Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
GLD closed at $322.87 on Nov 20, down from $369.36 on Nov 10 (-12.6%) and from $355.45 on Nov 13 (-9.2% on the week).
Spot gold ended the week near $3,535 an ounce, its lowest close in over a year.
Friday Nov 20 was the worst day: GLD -3.67% on about 23.6 million shares, roughly double its 10-day average.
Over the same week the 10-year Treasury yield fell from about 5.15% to 4.92%, and the 10-year real yield was nearly flat (2.91% to 2.88%).
Equities: the S&P 500 fell seven sessions in a row and the VIX closed near 36.
Silver fell more than 13% on the week.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Mechanism

My first explanation: the risk-free rate channel.

Gold pays no interest.
When real yields are high, holding gold means giving up more income.
Investors shift from gold to bonds, and gold falls.

Test against the data: yields fell last week, so this channel predicts gold flat or higher. Gold fell 9%. The rate story explains the decline since January, but not this week.
Revised explanation: the flows channel.

Equities fell sharply and volatility spiked.
Leveraged investors faced margin calls and needed cash.
They sold liquid assets, including gold, regardless of its fundamentals.
Evidence: double the normal volume, gold’s worst day matching the equity market’s worst day, and silver falling harder than gold.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Prediction


DRAFT, replace with my own number before publishing: 55% probability that GLD closes above $322.87 on Nov 30 (five trading days).
Reasoning: forced selling ends when the selling pressure in equities eases, even if yields do not move.
Wrong if GLD closes at or below $322.87 on Nov 30.
What I will watch: if the VIX falls and gold still declines, the flows explanation is wrong and rates or the dollar matter more than I think.
Disclosure: I hold a small position in GLD.
